// POST /orders: A's storm can't drain B's capacity
if !bh.sem.TryAcquire(1) { // the tenant's 5 permits are taken
ops._why: examples/12 per-tenant bulkhead on its library (S14); the slide is an excerpt

paragraphs: A bulkhead per tenant on golang.org/x/sync/semaphore: a Weighted semaphore of five per tenant, created on first use in a sync.Map. TryAcquire never waits, so a tenant that already has five orders in flight gets a 429 at once while every other tenant keeps its own five; the permit goes back in a deferred Release.

Refusing instead of queueing matters: a send on a full buffered channel, the other common Go idiom, blocks until a slot frees, which turns one tenant's storm into a pile of waiting goroutines. The atomic in-flight count feeds the bulkhead-state endpoint, since the semaphore does not report its own count.
